Main.sentence: George Walker Bush [a] (born July 6, 1946) is an American politician, businessman, and former ___E:U.S. Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Air_Force)___ officer who was the 43rd ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ from 2001 to 2009. A member of the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ and the eldest son of the 41st president, ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ , he served as the 46th ___E:governor of Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Texas)___ from 1995 to 2000.

Born into the prominent ___E:Bush family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_family)___ in ___E:New Haven, Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Haven,_Connecticut)___ , Bush flew warplanes in the ___E:Texas Air National Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Air_National_Guard)___ in his twenties.
After graduating from ___E:Harvard Business School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School)___ in 1975, he worked in the oil industry.

He later co-owned the ___E:Major League Baseball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball)___ team ___E:Texas Rangers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball))___ before being elected governor of Texas ___E:in 1994 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Texas_gubernatorial_election)___ . ___E:As governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governorship_of_George_W._Bush)___ , Bush successfully sponsored legislation for tort reform, increased education funding, set higher standards for schools, and reformed the criminal justice system.
He also helped make Texas the ___E:leading producer of wind-generated electricity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_power_in_Texas)___ in the United States.

In the ___E:2000 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election)___ , he won over Democratic incumbent vice president ___E:Al Gore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore)___ while ___E:losing the popular vote U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_elections_in_which_the_winner_lost_the_popular_vote)___ after a narrow and contested ___E:Electoral College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College)___ win, which involved ___E:a Supreme Court decision U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_v._Gore)___ to stop ___E:a recount in Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election_recount_in_Florida)___ .

In his first term, Bush signed ___E:a major tax-cut program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_tax_cuts)___ and an education-reform bill, the ___E:No Child Left Behind Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Child_Left_Behind_Act)___ .

He pushed for socially conservative efforts such as the ___E:Partial-Birth Abortion Ban Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial-Birth_Abortion_Ban_Act)___ and ___E:faith-based initiatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith-based_initiatives)___ .

He also initiated the ___E:President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President%27s_Emergency_Plan_for_AIDS_Relief)___ , in 2003, to address ___E:the AIDS epidemic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS_in_the_United_States)___ .

The ___E:terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ decisively reshaped his administration, resulting in the start of the ___E:war on terror U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror)___ and the creation of the ___E:Department of Homeland Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Homeland_Security)___ .

Bush ordered the ___E:invasion of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Afghanistan)___ in an effort to overthrow the ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ , destroy ___E:al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ , and capture ___E:Osama bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden)___ .
He signed the ___E:Patriot Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot_Act)___ to authorize surveillance of suspected terrorists.

He also ordered the ___E:2003 invasion of Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq)___ to overthrow ___E:Saddam Hussein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein)___ 's regime on the false belief that it ___E:possessed weapons of mass destruction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction)___ (WMDs) and had ___E:ties with al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein_and_al-Qaeda_link_allegations)___ .

Bush later signed the ___E:Medicare Modernization Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_Prescription_Drug,_Improvement,_and_Modernization_Act)___ , which created ___E:Medicare Part D U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_Part_D)___ .

In 2004, Bush ___E:was re-elected president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election)___ in a close race, beating Democratic opponent ___E:John Kerry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry)___ and winning the popular vote.

During his second term, Bush made various ___E:free trade agreements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade_agreement)___ , appointed ___E:John Roberts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Roberts)___ and ___E:Samuel Alito U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Alito)___ to the Supreme Court, and sought major changes to ___E:Social Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States))___ and immigration laws, but both efforts failed in Congress.

Bush was widely criticized for ___E:his administration's handling of Hurricane Katrina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criticism_of_the_government_response_to_Hurricane_Katrina)___ and revelations of ___E:torture against detainees at Abu Ghraib U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Ghraib_torture_and_prisoner_abuse)___ .
Amid his unpopularity, the Democrats regained control of Congress in the ___E:2006 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_United_States_elections)___ .
Meanwhile, the Afghanistan and Iraq wars continued; in January 2007, Bush launched ___E:a surge of troops in Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War_troop_surge_of_2007)___ .

By December, the U.S. entered the ___E:Great Recession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession)___ , prompting the Bush administration and Congress to push through economic programs intended to preserve the country's financial system, including the ___E:Troubled Asset Relief Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubled_Asset_Relief_Program)___ .
After his second term, Bush returned to Texas, where he has maintained a low public profile.
At various points in his presidency, he was among both the most popular and the most unpopular presidents in U.S. history.

He received the highest recorded approval ratings in the wake of the September 11 attacks, and one of the lowest ratings during the ___E:2008 financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis)___ .

Bush left office as one of the most unpopular U.S. presidents, with ___E:public opinion of him U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_image_of_George_W._Bush)___ remaining highly divisive. ___E:Scholars and historians rank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States)___ Bush as a below-average to the lower half of presidents. .mw-parser-output .toclimit-2 .toclevel-1 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-3 .toclevel-2 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-4 .toclevel-3 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-5 .toclevel-4 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-6 .toclevel-5 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-7 .toclevel-6 ul{display:none}

George Walker Bush was born on July 6, 1946, at ___E:Grace-New Haven Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace-New_Haven_Hospital)___ in ___E:New Haven, Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Haven,_Connecticut)___ .
He was the first child of ___E:George Herbert Walker Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Herbert_Walker_Bush)___ and ___E:Barbara Pierce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Pierce)___ .

He was raised in ___E:Midland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midland,_Texas)___ and ___E:Houston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston)___ , Texas, with four siblings: ___E:Jeb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Bush)___ , ___E:Neil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Bush)___ , ___E:Marvin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Bush)___ and ___E:Dorothy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Bush_Koch)___ .

Another younger sister, ___E:Robin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Robinson_Bush)___ , died from ___E:leukemia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leukemia)___ at the age of three in 1953.  His paternal grandfather, ___E:Prescott Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prescott_Bush)___ , was a U.S. senator from ___E:Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut)___ .

His father was ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ 's vice president from 1981 to 1989 and the 41st U.S. president from 1989 to 1993. Bush has ___E:English U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Americans)___ and ___E:German U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Americans)___ ancestry, along with more distant ___E:Dutch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Americans)___ , ___E:Welsh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_Americans)___ , ___E:Irish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Americans)___ , ___E:French U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Americans)___ , and ___E:Scottish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Americans)___ roots.  [improper synthesis?]
Bush attended public schools in Midland, Texas, until the family moved to Houston after he had completed seventh grade.

He then spent two years at ___E:The Kinkaid School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kinkaid_School)___ , a ___E:college-preparatory school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College-preparatory_school)___ in ___E:Piney Point Village, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piney_Point_Village,_Texas)___ .

Bush later attended ___E:Phillips Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillips_Academy)___ , a boarding school in ___E:Andover, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andover,_Massachusetts)___ , where he played baseball and was the head cheerleader during his senior year.   He attended ___E:Yale University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University)___ from 1964 to 1968, graduating with a ___E:Bachelor of Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ degree in history.

During this time, he was a cheerleader and a member of the ___E:Delta Kappa Epsilon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Kappa_Epsilon)___ , serving as the president of the fraternity during his senior year.    Bush became ___E:a member U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Skull_and_Bones_members)___ of the ___E:Skull and Bones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull_and_Bones)___ society as a senior.
Bush was a ___E:rugby union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union)___ player and was on Yale's 1st XV.  He characterized himself as an average student.

His ___E:grade point average U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_point_average)___ during his first three years at Yale was 77, and he had a similar average under a nonnumerical rating system in his final year.
In the fall of 1973, Bush entered ___E:Harvard Business School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School)___ .
He graduated in 1975 with a ___E:M.B.A. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration)___ degree, and is the only U.S. president to have earned the degree.
Bush was engaged to Cathryn Lee Wolfman in 1967, but the engagement did not last. Bush and Wolfman remained on good terms after the end of the relationship.
While Bush was at a backyard barbecue in 1977, friends introduced him to ___E:Laura Welch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Welch)___ , a schoolteacher and librarian.

After a three-month courtship, she accepted his marriage proposal and they wed on November 5 of that year.  The couple settled in ___E:Midland, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midland,_Texas)___ .

Bush left his family's ___E:Episcopal Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_Church_(United_States))___ to join his wife's ___E:United Methodist Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Methodist_Church)___ .

On November 25, 1981, Laura Bush gave birth to ___E:fraternal twin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraternal_twin)___ daughters, ___E:Barbara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Bush_(born_1981))___ and ___E:Jenna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Bush_Hager)___ .

Bush describes being challenged by ___E:Billy Graham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Graham)___ to consider faith in Jesus "Christ as the risen Lord", how he began to read the ___E:Bible U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible)___ daily, "surrendering" to the "Almighty", that "faith is a walk" and that he was "moved by ___E:God U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God)___ 's love".
Before his marriage, Bush repeatedly ___E:abused alcohol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_abuse)___ .

On September 4, 1976, he was pulled over near his ___E:family's summer home U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walker%27s_Point_Estate)___ in ___E:Kennebunkport, Maine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennebunkport,_Maine)___ , for ___E:driving under the influence of alcohol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_under_the_influence_of_alcohol)___ .
He was arrested for ___E:DUI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_under_the_influence)___ , was fined $150, and received a brief suspension of his Maine driver's license.
Bush said that his wife has had a stabilizing effect on his life,  and he attributes his decision to give up alcohol in 1986 to her influence.

While governor of Texas, Bush said of his wife, "I saw an elegant, beautiful woman who turned out not only to be elegant and beautiful, but very smart and willing to put up with my rough edges, and I must confess has smoothed them off over time."  Bush also says that his faith in God was critical in abstaining: "I believe that God helped open my eyes, which were closing because of booze".
Bush has been an avid reader throughout his adult life, preferring biographies and histories.

During his presidency, Bush read the Bible daily,  though at the end of his second term he said on television that he is "not a literalist" about Bible interpretation.   ___E:Walt Harrington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Harrington)___ , a journalist, recalled seeing "books by ___E:John Fowles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fowles)___ , ___E:F. Scott Fitzgerald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F._Scott_Fitzgerald)___ , ___E:James Joyce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Joyce)___ , and ___E:Gore Vidal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gore_Vidal)___ lying about, as well as biographies of ___E:Willa Cather U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willa_Cather)___ and ___E:Queen Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria)___ " in his home when Bush was a Texas oilman.
Other activities include cigar smoking and golf.  Bush has also painted many paintings.
One of his best-known projects is a collection of 43 paintings of immigrants, titled Out of Many, One .
Another painting project was Portraits of Courage: A Commander in Chief's Tribute to America's Warrior .

In May 1968, Bush joined the ___E:United States Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force)___ and was commissioned into the ___E:Texas Air National Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Air_National_Guard)___ .

After two years of training in active-duty service,  he was assigned to ___E:Houston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston)___ , flying ___E:Convair F-102s U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convair_F-102)___ with the ___E:147th Reconnaissance Wing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/147th_Reconnaissance_Wing)___ out of ___E:Ellington Field Joint Reserve Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellington_Field_Joint_Reserve_Base)___ .

Critics, including former ___E:Democratic National Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee)___ Chairman ___E:Terry McAuliffe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_McAuliffe)___ , have alleged that Bush was favorably treated due to his father's political standing as a member of ___E:the House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ , citing his selection as a pilot despite his low pilot aptitude test scores and his irregular attendance.

In June 2005, ___E:the Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ released all the records of Bush's Texas Air National Guard service, which remain in its official archives.

In late 1972 and early 1973, he drilled with the ___E:187th Fighter Wing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/187th_Fighter_Wing)___ of the ___E:Alabama Air National Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Air_National_Guard)___ .
He had moved to ___E:Montgomery, Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montgomery,_Alabama)___ , to work on the unsuccessful U.S.
Senate campaign of Republican ___E:Winton M. Blount U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winton_M._Blount)___ .

In 1972, Bush was suspended from flying for failure to take a scheduled physical exam.  He was honorably discharged from the ___E:Air Force Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Reserve)___ on November 21, 1974.
Bush remains the most recent president to have served in the military.

In 1977, Bush established ___E:Arbusto Energy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbusto_Energy)___ , a small ___E:oil exploration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_exploration)___ company, which began operations in 1978.   He later changed the name to Bush Exploration.
In 1984, his company merged with the larger ___E:Spectrum 7 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrum_7)___ , and Bush became chairman.

The company was hurt by decreased oil prices, and it folded into ___E:Harken Energy Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harken_Energy_Corporation)___ ,  with Bush becoming a member of Harken's board of directors.

Questions of ___E:possible insider trading U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush_insider_trading_allegations)___ involving Harken arose, but a ___E:Securities and Exchange Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities_and_Exchange_Commission)___ investigation concluded that the information Bush had at the time of his stock sale was not sufficient to constitute insider trading.

In April 1989, Bush arranged for a group of investors to purchase a controlling interest of Major League Baseball's ___E:Texas Rangers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball))___ for $89 million and invested $500,000 himself to start.
He then was managing general partner for five years.

He actively led the team's projects and regularly attended its games, often choosing to sit in the open stands with fans.  Bush's sale of his shares in the Rangers in 1998 brought him over $15 million from his initial $800,000 investment.

In the early or mid 1990s, before his gubernatorial campaign, Bush briefly considered a candidacy to become the ___E:Commissioner of Baseball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioner_of_Baseball)___ .

___E:In 1978 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)___ , Bush ran for the ___E:U.S. House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives)___ from ___E:Texas's 19th congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas%27s_19th_congressional_district)___ .

The retiring member, ___E:George H. Mahon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._Mahon)___ , had held the district for the Democratic Party since 1935. Bush's opponent, ___E:Kent Hance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent_Hance)___ , portrayed him as out of touch with rural Texans, and Bush lost the election, receiving 46.8 percent of the vote to Hance's 53.2 percent.

Bush and his family moved to Washington, D.C., in 1988 to work on ___E:his father's campaign for the U.S. presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush_1988_presidential_campaign)___ .
He was a campaign advisor and liaison to the media, and assisted his father by campaigning across the country.

In December 1991, Bush was one of seven people named by his father to run his father's 1992 presidential ___E:re-election campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush_1992_presidential_campaign)___ as a campaign advisor.
The previous month, his father had asked him to tell White House chief of staff ___E:John H. Sununu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_H._Sununu)___ to resign.

Bush declared his candidacy for the ___E:1994 Texas gubernatorial election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Texas_gubernatorial_election)___ at the same time his brother Jeb ___E:sought the governorship in Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Florida_gubernatorial_election)___ .
His campaign focused on four themes: welfare reform, ___E:tort reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tort_reform)___ , crime reduction, and education improvement.

Bush's campaign advisers were ___E:Karen Hughes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Hughes)___ , ___E:Joe Allbaugh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Allbaugh)___ , and ___E:Karl Rove U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Rove)___ .
After easily winning the Republican primary, Bush faced popular Democratic incumbent governor ___E:Ann Richards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Richards)___ .
In the course of the campaign, Bush pledged to sign a bill allowing Texans to obtain ___E:permits to carry concealed weapons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concealed_carry_permit)___ .
Richards had vetoed the bill, but Bush signed it into law after he became governor.

According to The Atlantic , the race "featured a rumor that she was a lesbian, along with a rare instance of such a tactic's making it into the public record – when a regional chairman of the Bush campaign allowed himself, perhaps inadvertently, to be quoted criticizing Richards for 'appointing avowed ___E:homosexual activists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_social_movements)___ ' to state jobs".
The Atlantic , and others, connected the lesbian rumor to Karl Rove,  but Rove denied being involved.
Bush won the general election with 53.5 percent of the vote against Richards' 45.9 percent.
Bush used a budget surplus to push through Texas's largest ___E:tax cut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_cut)___ , $2 billion.

He extended government funding for organizations providing education on the dangers of alcohol and ___E:drug use and abuse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substance_abuse)___ , and helping to reduce ___E:domestic violence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_violence)___ .
